terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static fence panel that tiles post to post. Both faces are seen and nothing is hollow, but nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A level builder places these in runs of dozens, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. The standard Thai house and land-plot boundary fence. ONE POST PER TILE: the post sits on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain post-bay-post-bay along X with no doubled post at a joint. The plate shows white paint greyed with dirt, black algae streaks along the slab joints, exposed grey concrete chips at the post corners and green moss along the bottom slab.

reasoning: ONE slotted square post with a plinth-and-pyramid cap and SEVEN horizontal plank slabs stacked from its slot to the +X edge; the slabs run from the ground to 0.90 H (proxy occupancy: slabs 0.00-0.90 H, caps 0.92-0.98 H, posts 6 of 80 columns).

Two materials: the slab concrete with a grime canvas carrying black joint streaks, an algae wash and a moss band, and the post concrete with a lighter grime canvas. A colour difference is not a material difference.
No repetition system: the seven courses differ only in height and are one merged extrusion set.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the root component, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the stacked horizontal joints and the moss-and-algae band at the bottom, delivered as chamfered slab edges (real shadow lines) and one height-keyed grime canvas per material.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 2.40 x 2.00 x 0.18 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static fence geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: one proxy over the whole panel envelope, which is what a run of fence collides as.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/slabmid.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. localOverrides.evidence: Moss carpet along the bottom courses in the plate (region-moss): a per-column moss wash under 26,000 fine tufts whose density follows a ragged sine-plus-random-walk top edge in the bottom 0.32 of a 2 m height-keyed tile, over a grey-green dirt wash and five ragged chips.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-slab (clean mid course, PBR confidence 0.860) at #d8d8d7; moss re-measured over 19,186 green plate pixels at mean #3d4417 (rows 640-920, top edge 0.55-0.8 m up the bay) and delivered as a linear-space ratio (#4f5e21 mat under multiplied tufts) in the grime canvas; black algae as a #292b24 band under every joint; bare concrete chips at #9a9a94.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px grime canvas is bound after construction as map and bumpMap.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 252/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory ~110 ms.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 4.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 252 of 4,000: boxes, two spikes and seven chamfered extrusions.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Tinted boxes for the posts and caps, a four-sided cone for each pyramid, chamfered-section extrusions for the slabs.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats at one size except the courses, which are already one merge.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. Two grime canvases after construction (512 and 256 px), 1.7 MB of texture VRAM, factory 67 ms.

risks.description: At 90 degrees the open +X end is the slab ends and the post behind them, 3.30% of the frame at the framing radius -- under the turntable segmenter's 3.5% floor (extract_pbr_evidence.build_foreground_mask), so that azimuth reports unsegmented and the gate FAILS regardless of colour; the first build cleared the floor by a hair and the 0.26 m cap moved the framing radius past it.
risks.mitigation: A property of a thin one-post tile seen from its open end: 0/180 segment at 1.00/1.005 and 270 (the post end) at 0.138 against the 0.05 collapse ratio. Recorded, not bypassed, as on the zinc and chain-link panels.

risks.description: The moss band reads as mottled specks rather than a carpet at the review distance.
risks.mitigation: Seventy soft clusters over a 0.45 wash; recorded, not hidden.

risks.description: Cap overhang makes the panel 0.22 m deep at the caps against the declared 0.18.
risks.mitigation: Proxy reads 0.245 m; the residual is the declared aspect and is reported.
